summary: Hiring cooled, oil stayed elevated, and borrowing costs remained near multi-decade highs while stocks traded close to record levels. The combination left markets balancing slower labor demand against persistent price pressure.

markets.name: S&P 500
markets.description: The Standard & Poor’s 500 (S&P 500) tracks large U.S. companies. Stocks in the index held near a record, and one common explanation is that slower hiring can lower expected interest rates, reducing a cost that investors use when valuing future profits.

explains.anchor_text: slower hiring can lower expected interest rates
explains.why: Lower expected rates can reduce what companies pay to borrow and can make future profits look more valuable today.
explains.other_reading: Slower hiring can also signal weaker growth, which can weigh on company earnings. Markets weigh both.

markets.name: 10-year Treasury yield
markets.description: The 10-year Treasury yield stayed close to a multi-decade high. Lenders often compare longer-term loans with Treasury rates, though borrower risk and competition also shape the final rate.

explains.anchor_text: Lenders often compare longer-term loans with Treasury rates
explains.why: Treasuries provide a widely observed baseline, and lenders add compensation for credit risk, servicing, and other costs.
explains.other_reading: Loan rates can diverge when competition, borrower quality, or market conditions change.

markets.gloss: A basis point is one-hundredth of a percentage point.

markets.name: Brent crude oil
markets.description: Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, eased after a volatile morning. Crude is one input in fuel, freight, and petroleum-based materials, though refining, taxes, inventories, and competition also affect final prices.

explains.anchor_text: Crude is one input in fuel, freight, and petroleum-based materials
explains.why: Oil is refined into fuels and materials, so crude-cost changes can move through transportation and production chains.
explains.other_reading: Refining margins, inventories, currency moves, taxes, and competition can offset or amplify the change households see.

markets.name: Gold futures
markets.description: Gold futures, contracts for delivery at a later date, moved higher. They can differ from the price of gold available for immediate delivery, known as the spot price.

markets.name: U.S. Dollar Index
markets.description: The U.S. Dollar Index (DXY), which compares the dollar with major currencies, strengthened. A firmer dollar can make some imports cheaper in dollar terms while making U.S. exports costlier for overseas buyers.

explains.anchor_text: A firmer dollar can make some imports cheaper
explains.why: Each dollar can buy more foreign currency, reducing the dollar cost of a foreign-priced item if sellers pass the change through.
explains.other_reading: Contracts, tariffs, shipping costs, and pricing decisions can limit or delay the effect.

markets.name: Expected volatility
markets.description: The Cboe Volatility Index (VIX), a measure of expected stock-market swings, moved higher. The change reflected pricier short-term protection, though the level remained below periods of severe market stress.

explains.why: The index is derived from S&P 500 options prices, which tend to rise when demand for protection or uncertainty increases.
explains.other_reading: Option prices also reflect positioning and market mechanics, so the index is not a direct measure of investor emotion.

calendar.title: Consumer Price Index (CPI)
calendar.definition: A measure of price changes for goods and services purchased by households.
calendar.hot: A higher-than-expected reading has often been associated with greater interest-rate pressure.
calendar.cool: A lower-than-expected reading has often been associated with less interest-rate pressure.

calendar.title: Producer Price Index (PPI)
calendar.definition: A measure of price changes received by domestic producers before many costs reach consumers.
calendar.hot: A higher-than-expected reading has often been associated with concern about future consumer-price pressure.
calendar.cool: A lower-than-expected reading has often been associated with easing business-cost pressure.

calendar.time: Decision at 2:00 p.m. ET on Oct. 28
calendar.title: Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting
calendar.definition: The Federal Reserve group that sets the target range for short-term interest rates.
calendar.hot: A tighter decision has often been associated with higher short-term borrowing costs.
calendar.cool: An unchanged rate has often been associated with more time for officials to assess inflation and employment.
